title: fix: harden DreamShaper Vast deployment
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Records DreamShaper instance `46607014` replacing `46307858` at `$0.150000/hr`, saving about `$18.40/month`, and reconciles the live Vast fleet burn.
- Adds a checked-in `setup-vast.sh` with isolated-canary defaults, explicit heartbeat/tunnel gates, `/root/onstart.sh`, and stale Uvicorn listener cleanup.
- Corrects the production pool key documentation (`sana`) and captures the successful deployment procedure.
- Documents validation: 210 images in 20.69s at 10.15 img/s, zero load errors, 1.54s p95, fixed-seed public parity, successful Vast stop/start, and 358 attributed production generations with zero backend failures before old-instance destruction.

Checks: `bash -n`, `git diff --check`. Biome processed no files because Markdown and shell are excluded. No model pricing, registry contract, production Worker deployment, or secret values changed.

gist.headline: DreamShaper gets a sturdier pot
gist.blurb: DreamShaper Vast has moved into a carefully checked new home, with canary gates, heartbeat checks, and a cleanup crew for stray Uvicorn listeners. The bees tested the plumbing before planting anything permanent.
gist.summary: Hardened the DreamShaper LCM Vast deployment around replacement instance 46607014 with a checked-in setup script, isolated-canary defaults, heartbeat and tunnel gates, stale Uvicorn cleanup, and documented validation procedures.
gist.impact: DreamShaper image generation now runs on a deployment path validated at 10.15 images/s with 1.54s p95 latency, fixed-seed public parity, successful stop/start recovery, and zero backend failures across 358 attributed production generations.
gist.visual_concept: Depict DreamShaper as a cozy image-generation garden greenhouse being carefully transplanted to a new, sturdier server plot. Polli wears a tiny mechanic tool belt and checks a glowing heartbeat meter and tunnel cable while a small CRT monitor robot watches a terminal showing clean image tiles; code-plants, flowers, and a gently cleared old cable suggest safe migration and reliable operations.
